_note: Covered regions. expected_trails is a collapse tripwire, self-baselined: the count this build measured on 13 Nov 2026 (California: 14 Nov 2026); the build fails if a region comes in under 50% of it. It is not an independent OSM figure. classics: each name must be found in the region's names.json with a length in len_m (metres), be ranked first by the app's own name search, and have a stored gain within max_err_pct (default 15) of published_ft (one-way headline gain in feet, source given). stored_len_m: range for the stored (stitched) length when it differs from names.json. v1: also publish the frozen old-format copy at trails/ (Washington only). max_err_pct above 15 is a temporary allowance and only goes with a known_bug note; remove both when the stitcher is fixed. published_len_mi (with len_source): the classic's published length in miles, one way for an out-and-back (half the round trip) or the loop; the stored length must be within 15% of it (max_len_err_pct to change), else the build fails unless len_exception explains a known definitional gap. Classic left out on purpose: Stawamus Chief (OpenStreetMap has no route or path covering a peak under that name; the peaks are separate spur ways named First, Second and Third Peak Trail, so no trailhead-to-summit gain can be checked). British Columbia's expected_trails (17626) is the count of its first CI build, 14 Nov 2026.

classics.name: Mount Si
classics.len_note: 8.0 mi round trip, halved (the text says a little under 4 mi one way).

classics.name: Dog Mountain Trails
classics.known_bug: known stitcher bug: chain starts away from the trailhead; remove when the stitcher is fixed
classics.detail: The stitched chain is 6.89 mi, the published loop length, but it dips to river level (the trailhead) mid-chain, adding a 1,128 ft up-and-down leg; trailhead to summit alone is 2,621 ft (-6.4%). Not DEM noise.
classics.len_note: The loop, 7.4 mi per that page (labelled round trip).

classics.name: Eagle Creek Trail
classics.note: Trailhead to Wahtum Lake: 1,500 ft over the first 7 miles plus 2,250 ft over the next 5, per that guide (sources vary).
classics.len_note: 7 mi plus 5 mi to Wahtum Lake; the page gives no total.

classics.name: Misery Ridge
classics.note: Loop figure (5.09 mi, 700 ft); other guides give 910 to 1,100 ft for the ridge climb.
classics.len_note: The guide says the climb section is about the next mile; the 5.09 mi in the gain note is the whole loop.

classics.name: Mist Trail
classics.note: Happy Isles to the top of Nevada Fall (the OSM relation ends there). National Park Service, Vernal Fall and Nevada Fall Trails: 5.4 mi round trip via the Mist Trail (2.7 mi one way) and 2,000 ft of gain. The Wikipedia infobox disagrees with this page, so it is not used. Gain to the top of Vernal Fall alone is about 1,000 ft.

classics.name: Steep Ravine Trail
classics.note: Mount Tamalpais area, from Pantoll: 3.96 mi out and back with 1,079 ft of gain per a commercial guide (The Outbound), so about 1.98 mi and that much descent one way. No state-park or NPS page gives this trail's own length and gain (California State Parks describes 1.5 mi downhill on it as part of a route to Stinson Beach); the Matt Davis Trail did not match any published figure.
classics.label: Steep Ravine Trail (Mount Tamalpais area)

classics.name: Four Mile Trail
classics.note: Yosemite Valley to Glacier Point: 4.8 mi one way, 3,200 ft gain, per the National Park Service.

classics.name: Mount Whitney Trail
classics.note: Whitney Portal to the summit: 10.7 mi per the National Park Service. Gain is derived from that page's trailhead (8,360 ft) and summit (14,505 ft) elevations, so it is a net figure.

classics.name: Cowles Mountain Trail
classics.note: San Diego: 3.0 mi round trip, about 1,000 ft of gain, per that article, so 1.5 mi one way. Third-party figures vary (855 to 1,030 ft).

classics.name: Grouse Grind
classics.note: Metro Vancouver's brochure: the trail climbs 800 m (2,625 ft). Other guides give 789 to 855 m. The OSM route relation is the Grind itself, about 1.9 km on the map.
classics.len_exception: Metro Vancouver's brochure gives the Grind as 2.5 km (about 1.55 mi); the OSM route is 1.92 km on the map. The gain matches, and the cause of the length gap is not established (other guides say 2.9 km).

classics.name: Garibaldi Lake
classics.note: Trailhead to the lake, one way: 9 km and about 900 m of gain per that guide (others give 810 to 900 m). OSM names the ways 'Garibaldi Lake Trail'. Length: 9 km one way.

classics.name: Wedgemount Lake
classics.note: One-way gain to the lake, 1,160 m per that guide (BC Parks' description gives a 1,200 m change over 7 km; other guides 1,220 to 1,250 m). OSM names the trail 'Wedgemount Lake Trail', 5.6 km mapped. Length: 12 km round trip per that guide (6 km one way, 3.73 mi); BC Parks' description says 7 km one way, which would put the map 20% short.
